A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Quantum Doubly Stochastic Transformers. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material that was reformatted or relocated.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, circuit expressivity and training ablations, numerical DSM enumeration, and quantum hardware measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a synthetic unit-hypersphere expressivity experiment.

M1.justification: The matrix-conditioned QontOT attention mechanism, QR alternative, circuit ansatz choices, and static, mixed, and differentiable training strategies are retained. Expanded explanations and revised resource accounting do not establish a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a targeted synthetic input scenario in which every matrix column has unit length. Application coverage remains unchanged: MNIST, FashionMNIST, the same seven MedMNIST datasets, Eureka, and IR spectra were already evaluated in v1, as were the three quantum backends.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 2B adds Softmax to the entropy–distance comparison corresponding to v1 Figure 3. The classification comparator sets remain unchanged. ESPFormer and LOTFormer are discussed but explicitly not evaluated.

E3.justification: The new hypersphere protocol enumerates 625 matrices at discretization d=3 with unit-length columns. The earlier injectivity check on 3,584 attention matrices from a trained Sinkformer is omitted. Retained classification protocols are unchanged; newly supplied split information documents existing experiments.

E4.justification: The added fixed-norm analysis tests whether operator collisions persist when column lengths are controlled, while the real-attention-batch collision analysis is removed. The entropy–distance analysis is revised. Existing circuit-depth, ansatz, optimization-strategy, and hardware-noise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-training mean/standard-deviation reporting, uncertainty bands, and five-fold cross-validation for IR spectra. The new checklist restates these practices without introducing additional runs, seeds, uncertainty procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The new hypersphere experiment reports 625 unique outputs for QontOT, 621 for Sinkhorn, and 381 for QR. The revised entropy–distance plot changes numerical values and rankings, with Birkhoff projection now having the smallest distance. The absolute distance scale changes without an explained setting change, so it does not establish a same-setting performance improvement. Main benchmark means are retained.

T1.justification: The DSM-counting derivations remain unchanged after moving from Appendix D to E. However, Section 3.1 adds the assertion f(λA)=f(A) for all operators and broadens Sinkhorn scale-invariance beyond v1's Naive-only qualification. The blanket assertion conflicts with v2's subsequent statement that QontOT is not scale-invariant.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: parametric quantum doubly stochastic attention, the QR alternative, greater expressivity, improved classification, and training stability. The introduction's more explicit Eureka claim was already present in v1's results and conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 changes QontOT's information preservation from superior to comparable to Sinkhorn and drops the claim that it is best among all operators. v2 also explicitly qualifies injectivity as empirically observed rather than proven and explains collisions through row-constant rank-one inputs.

D1.justification: v2 adds software versions, POWER8 hardware and approximate training times, split details, baseline implementation links, backend specifications, and dataset sizes/licenses. Its checklist newly states that the full code cannot be public and that specific parts are available upon justified request. These are documentation and access disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing training settings.

R1.justification: v2 expands the discussion of the already-cited ESPFormer and adds LOTFormer, explicitly explaining their exclusion from experiments. It also adds references concerning Sinkhorn initialization and optimization, Birkhoff projection, and quantum architectures. The fundamental research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main six-section narrative and most prose remain intact, with localized rewrites and expanded explanations. The hardware appendix moves to the beginning of the appendices, and v2 adds correspondence information, declarations, author contributions, and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The document switches throughout from two-column to single-column layout. v1 Tables 1–2 become one table, Figures 2–3 become a combined figure with a revised plot, and the Eureka table and curve become Figure 4. Hardware plots move to the appendix, while backend and dataset tables and an author-contribution graphic are added.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a useful fixed-norm expressivity check, improves implementation and access documentation, and gives a more cautious body-level interpretation of the revised distance evidence. These provide limited gains while preserving the main empirical contribution. The improvement is constrained by the contradictory scale-invariance statements and by the abstract and conclusion retaining stronger information-preservation claims than the revised analysis supports.
